title: The integral constructible category and its heart
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell$ be a prime different from $p$, and let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Coefficients are the completed ring sheaf $R_X=\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and the ambient category is the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use the constructibility and bounded constructibility of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the standard truncations of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and the fixed-universe size convention [def-weil-size-convention].

1. $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is a full triangulated subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Its objects are bounded, and it is stable under the standard truncations.
2. $\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ identifies with the objects of $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ concentrated in degree $0$. It is an abelian full subcategory of $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$: kernels and cokernels of its morphisms, computed in $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$, belong to it. It is closed under extensions and essentially small (its isomorphism classes form a set in the chosen universe).

proof.text: Put $R=R_X$ and $\kappa=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E$. The residue field $\kappa$ is finite by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](3), and $\pi_E\mathcal O_E=\mathfrak m_E$ by the choice of uniformizer. By [sk-lem-integral-models](2), an ambient $R$-complex belongs to $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ if and only if it is derived complete and its derived reduction $K_1=K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\kappa_X$ is a bounded constructible complex pulled back from the étale site. This is a theorem identifying the cohomological definition with the residue criterion, not a redefinition of $\Dbc$. Its hypotheses hold: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian because the only ideals of the field $k$ are $0$ and $k$. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to the structure morphism to obtain local Noetherianity of $X$. Its finite-type hypothesis makes $X$ quasi-compact, since the inverse image of the affine target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is all of $X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $X$ is Noetherian, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite as required. The zero complex satisfies both conditions and hence belongs to $\Dbc$.

source.place: Paragraph (1), the two defining conditions, with the comparison in unit proof paragraph 1 made explicit

proof.text: For $K\in\Dbc$, its shifts $K[n]$ remain derived complete by [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction]. Derived scalar extension is an exact triangulated functor by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2), so $(K[n])_1\simeq K_1[n]$. Bounded intrinsically constructible finite-coefficient complexes are shift-stable by [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated]. Every such bounded complex has bounded constructible étale origin by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], applied to the finite commutative ring $\kappa$. Thus the residue criterion of step 1 gives $K[n]\in\Dbc$ for every integer $n$.

Let $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ be an ambient distinguished triangle with $K,M\in\Dbc$. Rotate it to $M[-1]\to K\to L\to M$. By step 2 and cone closure of derived complete complexes [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction], $L$ is derived complete. Apply exact derived reduction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to the original triangle. The outer vertices $K_1,M_1$ have bounded constructible cohomology. The outer-vertex closure in [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] gives the same for $L_1$. The finite-ring origin theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] supplies its bounded constructible étale representative. Hence [sk-lem-integral-models](2) gives $L\in\Dbc$. This works for arbitrary ambient triangles and morphisms. Together with zero and all shifts, it is precisely the full-triangulated-subcategory criterion of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], so the ambient distinguished triangles and shifts give the asserted triangulation and exact inclusion.

source.place: Paragraph (1), stability under cones and conclusion that Dbc is triangulated

proof.text: Boundedness is already part of the current cohomological definition [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: $\Dbc$ consists of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves. This avoids applying a bounded-reduction assertion without its completeness hypothesis. Both standard truncations remain in $\Dbc$ by [det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model](3). By the same definition a module placed in degree zero belongs to $\Dbc$ exactly when it belongs to $\Cons$. Conversely, if $K\in\Dbc$ has cohomology only in degree zero, [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] with $r=0$ identifies $K$ with $H^0(K)[0]$. Its cohomology is constructible by the definition. The degree-zero single-complex functor is fully faithful by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]. Thus it identifies the full module category $\Cons$ with precisely the full subcategory of degree-zero objects of $\Dbc$, including all their morphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (1), boundedness and standard truncations; paragraph (2), identification of the degree-zero subcategory

proof.text: Let $f:C\to C'$ be a morphism of constructible $R$-modules and let $D$ be its cone in the ambient derived category. The triangulation proved above, rotated if necessary, implies $D\in\Dbc$. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] of $C[0]\to C'[0]\to D\to C[1]$ reads $0\to H^{-1}(D)\to C\xrightarrow f C'\to H^0(D)\to0$, since $C[0],C'[0]$ have no other cohomology. Thus the ambient kernel is $H^{-1}(D)$ and the ambient cokernel is $H^0(D)$. By [det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model](2) these sheaves placed in degree zero lie in $\Dbc$, so step 4 puts both in $\Cons$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), kernels and cokernels of a morphism

proof.text: The full subcategory $\Cons$ contains zero and finite direct sums: the cone formula of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes the cone of the zero map $C[-1]\to C'$ equal to $C'\oplus C$ in degree zero, so the triangulation and the degree-zero identification already proved put it in $\Cons$. It inherits addition on morphisms from modules. The kernel and cokernel from step 5 have their ambient universal properties in this full subcategory. Its images and coimages are therefore the ambient ones, and their canonical comparison is an ambient isomorphism with inverse again a morphism of the full subcategory. Hence $\Cons$ is abelian. For an ambient short exact sequence $0\to C'\to C\to C''\to0$ with constructible ends, [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] applied to the degree-zero complexes gives a distinguished triangle $C'[0]\to C[0]\to C''[0]\to C'[1]$. Step 3 puts $C[0]$ in $\Dbc$ and step 4 puts $C$ in $\Cons$, proving closure under ambient extensions.

source.place: Paragraph (2), abelianness and closure under extensions

proof.text: We now supply the set of local data rather than assuming it classifies global gluings. Fix one stratum $S$. In the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], its pro-étale site has a fixed small skeleton [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. By [sk-def-sfb-constructible](1), a finite constant local model sheaf is locally $\mathcal O_{E,U}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}P$ for a finitely presented scalar module $P$. Representatives for such $P$ form a set: use the cokernels of all finite matrices over the set $\mathcal O_E$. Cover families in a small site can be chosen from a set (discard repeated arrows), and assignments of these scalar presentations form a set. For each overlap $W=U_i\times_SU_j$, an overlap module map between the fixed model sheaves $A,B$ is a family in $\prod_{(V\to W)}\operatorname{Map}(A(V),B(V))$, subject to naturality and linearity; the index is the object set of a small slice site and all factors are sets in the chosen universe. Invertibility imposes a further condition on this set of maps. Thus the overlap isomorphisms also form a set. These data determine a sheaf up to isomorphism: for two realizations with the same data, at every test object $V\to S$ use the local identifications on $V\times_SU_i$ and their overlap agreement to glue a unique map on sections; glue their inverses in the same way. The equalizer sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) proves these maps are inverse and natural, and they are module-linear locally and hence globally. The module structures and morphisms are the sectionwise ones of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Consequently there is a set of isomorphism classes of finite constant local model sheaves on each fixed $S$. No effectivity assertion for arbitrary data is needed: retain only data that have a realization.

source.place: Paragraph (2), essential smallness: finite presentations and pro-étale cover data

proof.text: For a finite stratification $(a_s:S_s\to X)_s$ and chosen local-model sheaves $F_s$ from step 7, put $P=\prod_s a_{s*}F_s$, a finite product of $R$-module sheaves. These are the module direct images and adjunctions $a_s^*\dashv a_{s*}$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], with the pulled-back coefficient identifications of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1). Its final assertion makes every $a_s^*$ exact and canonically naturally isomorphic to the lift of $a_s^{-1}$ on underlying abelian sheaves, with the $\mathcal O_{E,S_s}$-action obtained through $\alpha_{a_s}^{-1}$. Here we use only the untwisted admissible coefficient $\mathcal O_E$, so none of the extra hypotheses for the Tate-twist clause is needed. For a constructible $C$, choose isomorphisms $\varphi_s:a_s^*C\xrightarrow{\sim}F_s$. Define $u:C\to P$ by its components $u_s=a_{s*}(\varphi_s)\circ\eta_{s,C}$, where $\eta_s$ is the adjunction unit. Let $N=\ker u$. For each $s$, exactness of $a_s^*$ makes $a_s^*N$ the kernel of $a_s^*u$. The component $a_s^*u_s:a_s^*C\to a_s^*a_{s*}F_s$ has the explicit left inverse $\varepsilon_{s,a_s^*C}\circ a_s^*a_{s*}(\varphi_s^{-1})$, where $\varepsilon_s$ is the adjunction counit: its composite with $a_s^*u_s$ is $\varepsilon_{s,a_s^*C}\circ a_s^*\eta_{s,C}=\mathrm{id}_{a_s^*C}$ by the triangle identity. Thus $a_s^*u_s$ is monic; since it is a component of $a_s^*u$, that map has zero kernel. Hence $a_s^*N=0$ for every $s$. The precise underlying-sheaf identification above therefore gives $a_s^{-1}U(N)=0$ for every $s$, where $U$ forgets the module action. The finite-stratum zero-detection statement [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection], applied to $U(N)$ with the identity covers on the strata and the Noetherianity proved in step 1, gives $U(N)=0$, hence $N=0$. Thus $C\to P$ is monic. Notice that we only need the split monomorphism furnished by the adjunction, not a claim that $a_s^*a_{s*}$ is the identity.

source.place: Paragraph (2), essential smallness: explicit determination by stratum data and global gluing

proof.text: There is a set of finite stratifications of the fixed scheme $X$: the locally closed subsets form a set, and their bounded scheme structures and immersion maps are sets in the chosen universes. Step 7 gives a set of possible tuples $(F_s)_s$ for each stratification, hence a set of possible sheaves $P$ in step 8. For each fixed $P$, its subobjects form a set directly: kernels of module sheaf morphisms are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so a monomorphism is sectionwise injective; identify it with its image subsheaf. Such an image is specified by a subset of $P(V)$ for each object $V$ of the fixed small site, subject to the module, restriction and sheaf axioms. All such choices lie in the set $\prod_V\mathcal P(P(V))$. Therefore subobjects of all these $P$ form a set, and by step 8 they contain representatives of every constructible sheaf. Its isomorphism classes form a set, as required. For the empty scheme, the empty stratification gives the terminal, zero module sheaf and the same argument applies.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence that the data form a set; expanded subobject count

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported two-paragraph proof into nine steps using existing nodes only. Made the standing geometric and coefficient hypotheses explicit; used the actual integral-model equivalence rather than treating completeness as a definition. Cited finite-coefficient triangulation and étale origin separately. Verified the cone kernel/cokernel identifications and ambient extension triangle. Replaced unspecified global gluing data by an explicit adjunction-unit monomorphism and a sectionwise subobject count. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves. The final clause audit also cites concentration and single-complex full faithfulness to justify the heart identification on objects and morphisms. Second reading adds the explicit Noetherianity citation and counts overlap morphisms sectionwise; no new nodes. Landing-refusal repair (2026-10-17): re-read all 23 cited proof-node statements against the current DAG; refreshed the obsolete cartesian-coefficients quote; step 8 now explicitly uses its canonical underlying-sheaf natural isomorphism and applies stratum zero detection to the underlying abelian sheaf. No statement, route, new-node or hypothesis change. Independent second reading: wrote the stratum-unit map and its retraction using the chosen local-model isomorphism explicitly; all 34 quotations revalidated.
split_report.blueprint: Proof paragraph (1) realized by steps 1–4: completeness, exact reduction, finite constructibility, triangulation, boundedness and truncations. Paragraph (2) realized by steps 5–6 for the abelian heart and extensions, and steps 7–9 for the finite presentation/cover/gluing-data size argument. The chapter and unit route are preserved.

tool_uses.why: Finiteness of the residue field permits application of the finite-ring constructibility tools; this is a generic coefficient-field fact.
Cone and shift closure for derived completeness; the integral-heart unit invokes these as generic completion facts.
Exactness of derived reduction as a ringed-site scalar-extension functor; no heart-unit statement supplies that functorial exactness.
Triangulation for the finite residue-field complexes used in the unit residue-reduction route.
Bounded finite-coefficient intrinsic constructibility has étale origin; keeps the actual hypothesis of the integral-model criterion.
The ambient long exact sequence identifies the kernel and cokernel; a general derived-category tool.
An ambient short exact sequence of degree-zero complexes gives its distinguished triangle.
Exact module inverse images for the actual pulled-back integral coefficients, used only in the size argument.
Joint zero detection of finite stratum restrictions proves the global adjunction-unit map is monic; no integral-heart-unit statement supplies it.
The general concentration theorem identifies a complex with only H^0 with a degree-zero module; it makes essential surjectivity of the heart identification explicit.
Full faithfulness of the single-complex functor identifies the morphisms of the degree-zero subcategory with module morphisms.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q20-14671086d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 8 statement dependencies and all 23 proof dependencies in full, plus the blueprint's triangulated, unit and local-model proof texts and Stacks proetale.tex 09C1/09C2. The coefficient category is D(Mod(R_X)) with R_X = p_X^* O_E throughout; completeness, Nakayama and integral-models(2) are all stated for R_X, and the item never identifies R_X with the constant sheaf C_X. Step 1: integral-models(2) is an actual if-and-only-if, the residue field is finite, and X is Noetherian. Steps 2-3: shift and cone closure of derived completeness, exact reduction to kappa, the finite-ring triangulation lemma, and both directions of the étale-origin equivalence; the item rightly does not use the 09C2 boundedness shortcut, since 09C2 assumes finite tor dimension. Step 4: boundedness holds by the cohomological definition and the degree-zero identification is correct. Step 5: kernel and cokernel are H^{-1} and H^0 of the cone, checked on a zero map and an isomorphism. Step 6: the cone of zero gives direct sums, and short exact sequences give triangles. Steps 7-9: the uniqueness-of-gluing argument, the split adjunction unit and stratum zero detection with identity covers are correct, and the subobject count is valid. Edge cases checked: empty X, and multiplication by pi on O_{E,X}. There are no new nodes, no cycle (the item is not reachable from anything it cites) and no duplicate (det-lem-coefficient-heart-small covers only E and Qlbar; prop-constructible-truncations covers another category). I accept the 11 declared generic tool_uses. Caution for later, not a fault here: the blueprint proof of local-model(3) uses this item's clause 1, so whoever splits det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model must prove (2) and (3) directly from the cohomological definition, not by citing this item. No fixes.
